import pandas as pd
from datetime import timedelta

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract high_ts from watermark (single row)
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter events with event_ts > high_ts
    new_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # Sort by user_id, then event_ts, then event_seq for deterministic processing
    new_events = new_events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Create a dictionary from target_snapshot for quick lookup
    snapshot_dict = {}
    for _, row in target_snapshot.iterrows():
        user_id = row["user_id"]
        snapshot_dict[user_id] = {
            "email": row["email"],
            "status": row["status"],
            "status_ts": row["status_ts"]
        }
    
    # Process each event sequentially per user
    for _, event in new_events.iterrows():
        user_id = event["user_id"]
        event_ts = event["event_ts"]
        op = event["op"]
        email = event["email"]
        
        if user_id not in snapshot_dict:
            # New user
            if op == "U":
                snapshot_dict[user_id] = {
                    "email": email,
                    "status": "ACTIVE",
                    "status_ts": event_ts
                }
            # op 'D' on non-existent user is ignored or creates deleted record
            # Assuming we create it
            elif op == "D":
                snapshot_dict[user_id] = {
                    "email": email,
                    "status": "DELETED",
                    "status_ts": event_ts
                }
        else:
            # User exists
            current = snapshot_dict[user_id]
            
            if op == "D":
                # Soft delete: preserve email, set status to DELETED
                current["email"] = email
                current["status"] = "DELETED"
                current["status_ts"] = event_ts
            
            elif op == "U":
                if current["status"] == "ACTIVE":
                    # Active user: apply update
                    current["email"] = email
                    current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                    current["status_ts"] = event_ts
                elif current["status"] == "DELETED":
                    # Deleted user: check resurrection window
                    deletion_ts = current["status_ts"]
                    # Resurrection allowed if event_ts > deletion_ts + 7 days (strict inequality)
                    resurrection_threshold = deletion_ts + timedelta(days=7)
                    
                    if event_ts > resurrection_threshold:
                        # Resurrect
                        current["email"] = email
                        current["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                        current["status_ts"] = event_ts
                    # else: within 7-day window, discard the update (deletion is sticky)
    
    # Convert snapshot_dict back to DataFrame
    result_rows = []
    for user_id, data in snapshot_dict.items():
        result_rows.append({
            "user_id": user_id,
            "email": data["email"],
            "status": data["status"],
            "status_ts": data["status_ts"]
        })
    
    new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure correct dtypes
    if len(new_snapshot) > 0:
        new_snapshot["user_id"] = new_snapshot["user_id"].astype("int64")
        new_snapshot["email"] = new_snapshot["email"].astype("object")
        new_snapshot["status"] = new_snapshot["status"].astype("object")
        new_snapshot["status_ts"] = new_snapshot["status_ts"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    else:
        new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(columns=["user_id", "email", "status", "status_ts"])
        new_snapshot = new_snapshot.astype({
            "user_id": "int64",
            "email": "object",
            "status": "object",
            "status_ts": "datetime64[us]"
        })
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
